status: Reviewed source-fit authoring design using unchanged existing claims; not observed learner performance.

contributors.role: Whole grid-reference construction/interpretation and directional location/path operation.
Actual two-dimensional map/key/label interpretation and creation; retained complete prerequisite checked separately, not inferred from a source link.

resources.actualReadback: Actual one-page PDF visually inspected, including province/territory boundaries, capital/other-place key and selected Ontario/Quebec/Manitoba labels.
limits: Use the actual political labels and key, not outdated magnetic-pole or ice annotations as current scientific data.
The named political map does not establish Indigenous territories or precise legal boundaries.
No exact distance, density or full13capital recall is inferred by this grid task.

resources.actualReadback: Actual current national Regions layer/text/legend previously read/visually inspected for the selected Canadian Shield, Hudson Bay Lowland and Great Lakes–StLawrence Lowlands.
limits: Keep the stated current regional convention. Physical regions and political regions are different kinds of areas.
Do not stretch different projections into one falsely precise overlay.

preparation: Provide the actual political map in print and the actual physical-region reference in a digital view, with their legible keys and chosen labels. Also prepare an ORIGINAL clearly labelled schematic of selected political and physical-region locators using verified broad positions. It is a teaching diagram, not a surveyed boundary map. Give it a declared local north direction and an eight-point rose; do not assume page-up is geographic north across every projected Canada map.

Prepare a numbered-row/lettered-column grid on both a printed and a digital selected map/diagram. Keep the grid and the actual map reference together. A cell name refers to a cell or marked locator, not a point-coordinate system or a claim an entire large province fits one square.

Select Ontario/Quebec/Manitoba political labels and the three reviewed physical regions. For large/multi-cell regions, ask for a stated marked locator or an actual set of intersecting cells; make the target unit explicit and accept all supported cells. Do not infer national inventory mastery from locating supplied labels.
actions: Teach/review north, south, east, west and the four intermediate directions northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest using the stated north reference. After study, have the learner identify/name all eight and explain between which cardinal directions each intermediate lies; do not reduce the source requirement to only four points.

Use different printed and digital views to locate selected political AND physical regions with the actual labels/key. Name a specified grid cell or cells/locator for each and give a supported directional relationship under the declared diagram reference. Distinguish a region’s label/locator from the extent of the entire region.

Rotate the original schematic while preserving its geographic north indication. Locate the same features and explain a changed page-relative position using the unchanged geographic directions; pointing to the top of the page regardless of the north reference is insufficient. This diagram exercise does not pretend the source maps share a projection or a single globally vertical north.

For the complete unchanged grid claim, create a small letter/number cell grid over a familiar park/classroom plan, list grid addresses for at least three features and describe a route using grid references and directions. Preserve the full earlier map/key/label requirement by drawing a familiar-place map from above, adding a key/landmark labels and explaining relative locations. These whole-claim checks remain separate from identifying supplied Canadian names.

Transfer to a differently styled print/digital map with a changed grid origin/labels and a declared north reference. Explain why the same place can receive a different grid address without moving, and locate selected region labels/locators accurately rather than memorize one colour or address.
protocol.positive: Demonstrates all eight directions and uses them with number/letter cell references to locate selected political and physical regions across actual print/digital maps, with complete map/grid creation and changed-view checks.
nearMiss: Calls the page top north after the schematic rotates away from its north arrow.
Gives a point coordinate when asked for a named cell, or assumes a whole region occupies only its label’s square.
Uses only a printed map and merely names a digital app.
Claims the capital/province knowledge inventory is mastered because a supplied name was found in a cell.

performanceConditions.gridUnit: letter-number cells; marked-locator or intersecting-region cells explicitly specified
performanceConditions.northReference: declared local reference; preserved under original-diagram rotation

limits: No magnetic mechanism, compass-instrument calibration, latitude/longitude numerical calculation, formal scale-drawing or new8-point topic is imported.
Actual region names can be supplied for this spatial-operation task. Canadian name/capital knowledge remains independently qualified elsewhere.
The design is untested authoring coverage, not a delivered software lesson or observed learner performance.

readiness: Grid → map creation → familiar plan → positional language are unchanged hard paths. The complete grid/map tasks check actual prerequisite performance. Finding places on a plan has global end age9 and no new CA9–10 context here: runtime selection readiness is a separate consumer concern, not repaired by fabricated prerequisite associations or changed ages. The authoring protocol can assess those skills without asserting learner mastery.
boundary: Two exact CA/Ontario9–10contexts are proposed, preserving all old contexts and complete claims. Existing generic directions/grid operations genuinely contribute; the four extra direction names required by the source are taught/checked in the protocol, not a new grade/difficulty clone.
